A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Safe In-Context Reinforcement Learning work. The complete main texts, figures, tables, algorithms, proofs, and appendices support comparison, including matching EPPO in v1 to SCARED in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original SafeDarkRoom and SafeDarkMujoco experiments, budget-response evaluations, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on the retained environments and added SafeVelocity tasks, including baseline comparisons and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, line 35, changes the written multiplier update from accumulating maximum episode cost to accumulating maximum episode cost minus the budget δ. This corrects a procedural step to match the retained mathematical update. The exact-penalty objective, actor-critic architecture, and policy conditioning otherwise remain; EPPO becomes SCARED.

E1.justification: v2 retains SafeDarkRoom and SafeDarkMujoco Point/Car and adds SafeVelocity HalfCheetah/Ant experiments with held-out target velocities. This adds locomotion tasks and an unseen in-distribution evaluation regime alongside the existing obstacle-and-goal distribution shifts.

E2.justification: Figures 1–2 add MAML with penalty and SafeMeta to comparisons on both retained and added environments. v1 compared EPPO with safe supervised pretraining, renamed safe AD in v2. The appendix AD-EPS and naive primal-dual comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Continuous-control safe AD changes from 50,000 collection steps at each of three cost limits to 2–5 million steps at cost limit zero. Its embedding dimension increases from 64 to 512, and Point context length changes from 300 to 200. Main adaptation evaluations replace fixed safe AD RTG/CTG targets with 100 paired targets and narrow SCARED's SafeDarkRoom CTG range from [1,15] to [1,10]. New velocity and meta-RL evaluation protocols are also introduced.

E4.justification: Figure 2 extends the budget-sensitivity analysis to SafeMeta, MAML with penalty, and the velocity tasks, adding evidence about their budget responsiveness. The noise-distillation comparison and context-length, model-size, dataset-size, and optimizer ablations in Appendices D–E retain their underlying curves.

E5.justification: Both versions report task-averaged curves with standard-error shading. Added comparisons use the same uncertainty-reporting practice; neither version reports independent training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 add velocity-task and meta-RL results and replace the continuous-control safe AD curves. For Point, late safe AD return is now approximately 0.3 with cost around 11, versus v1's low, erratic returns and costs below 1. These are results under changed training and evaluation settings, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains. Appendix D–E curves are retained.

T1.justification: The substantive CMDP formulation, exact-penalty surrogate, Assumptions 1–2, Theorem 1, Proposition 1, and Appendix B proofs are retained. Renumbering and reordered theorem clauses do not change their mathematical content. The added convergence caveat qualifies scope without supplying or revising a proof.

C1.justification: The central claims of safe, parameter-update-free adaptation and budget-responsive behavior remain. v2 centers its contributions on SCARED, presents safe supervised pretraining as the safe AD baseline, and explicitly extends claimed superiority to safe meta-RL methods and applicability to unseen in-distribution tasks.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking meta-RL failures to absent cross-episode histories and larger offline data requirements to diverse cost experiences and RTG/CTG combinations. Appendix B.1 explicitly places full convergence outside scope, while Appendix C removes v1's warning about infeasible environments causing excessive multipliers. Section 5.4 also adds a near-universal budget-compliance interpretation that Figure 2's maximum-cost curves do not establish.

D1.justification: Appendix C and new Table 2 provide substantial SafeMeta/MAML architecture, task-sampling, adaptation, and optimizer details; data-collection instructions and safe AD hyperparameters are revised. However, v1's explicit 16-task evaluation count and multiplier-capping guidance disappear. SafeVelocity training is inconsistently reported as 1,000 updates in Section 5.2 and 10,000 in Table 1. v2 claims benchmark/protocol release without providing an access link.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning around Finn et al.'s MAML and Xu and Zhu's SafeMeta, and cites Fu et al. when discussing offline dataset scale. It removes v1's explicit positioning of RCPO as the closest method. The main novelty distinction between safe ICRL and parameter-updating safe meta-RL remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v2 separates problem formulation from the proposed method, moves safe AD into the baseline section, and organizes experiments into setup, generalization, and analysis subsections. It also adds a Broader Impacts Statement and consistently renames the approaches.

P2.justification: The document changes from one-column to two-column formatting. Figures 1–2 replace separate method panels and dual axes with environment columns, separate return/cost rows, and shared comparator legends. v2 adds a baseline hyperparameter table, regroups existing tables, restyles Figure 4, and places Figures 5–6 together.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the empirical comparison more informative through established safe meta-RL comparators, a stronger continuous-control safe AD setup, and more consistent budget sweeps. Corrected pseudocode and comparative figures also help. The net improvement is limited by lost feasibility and sample-size disclosures, conflicting SafeVelocity training counts, and budget-compliance language stronger than the displayed evidence supports.
